1.title: Quick-Reference Recap and Service Chooser
1.text: Welcome to Module fifteen: the Quick-Reference Recap and Service Chooser. There is no new content here. This module puts the whole course on a few pages: look-alike ideas and services side by side, a chooser that maps a need to a service, and the lists and terms the exam likes. Use it in your last week, and say the answers aloud.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. See the whole exam on one page: the domains, the weights, and where each topic lives. Tell look-alike ideas and services apart, in pairs and sets. Use a need-to-service chooser for questions that describe a need. And recall the lists the exam likes, and the terms that trip people up.

1.title: Case Check-In: Cedar and Salt's Final Review
1.text: Cedar and Salt's assistant now has models, prompts, its own data, evaluation, safeguards and an audit trail. Before the exam, you want one page per topic, not fourteen modules. Some look-alikes keep getting mixed up: R A G and fine-tuning, Clarify and Guardrails, Config and CloudTrail. Your job is to review quickly, and fix the confusions that cost points.

1.title: The Exam on One Page
1.text: Here is the exam on one page. Fundamentals of A I and M L is twenty percent, in modules one to three: the concepts, the A W S A I services, and the lifecycle with metrics. Fundamentals of generative A I is twenty-four percent, in modules four to six: tokens, embeddings, agents, strengths and limits, and the A W S platforms. Applications of foundation models is twenty-eight percent, in modules seven to ten: R A G, prompting, fine-tuning and evaluation. Responsible A I is fourteen percent, and security, compliance and governance is fourteen percent. Sixty-five questions, ninety minutes, seven hundred to pass. Exam tip: the first three domains carry seventy-two percent, but the smaller ones are still worth the points.

1.title: Look-Alikes: AI and ML Concepts
1.text: First, concept look-alikes. A I is the umbrella; M L learns from data; deep learning uses neural networks; generative A I creates content; and agentic A I acts toward goals. Supervised learning uses labels, unsupervised finds patterns, and reinforcement uses rewards. Classification predicts categories, regression predicts numbers, and clustering finds groups. Training builds the model, and inference uses it. Real-time is instant, serverless is on demand, asynchronous suits large or slow jobs, and batch handles many at once. Underfitting is high bias, and overfitting is high variance. Exam tip: say the one-line job of each term before you look at the options.

1.title: Look-Alikes: AWS AI Services
1.text: Next, the A W S A I services. Transcribe turns speech into text, Polly turns text into speech, and Translate converts language to language. Comprehend finds meaning in text, and Textract pulls text and fields from scanned documents. Rekognition analyzes images and video, Lex builds chatbots, and Personalize makes recommendations. Amazon SageMaker A I builds, trains and deploys your own models. Amazon Bedrock gives foundation models through one A P I. JumpStart offers pre-trained and open models to deploy and tune. Autopilot builds models automatically, DataBrew cleans data without code, and Model Monitor checks for drift. Exam tip: pre-built A I services do one task, and SageMaker A I is for your own models.

1.title: Look-Alikes: GenAI Platforms and Tools
1.text: Now generative A I platforms and tools. Bedrock offers the least effort and many providers; SageMaker A I offers the most control. Knowledge Bases is managed R A G, Guardrails filters content, and Prompt Management keeps versioned prompts. Strands Agents is an S D K to code agents, and AgentCore is a service to run and govern them. Agents Classic is the earlier Bedrock Agents service, closed to new sign-ups. Amazon Nova is Amazon's own family of foundation models. Quick gives work insights, Kiro is an A I development environment, and A W S Transform modernizes code. On-demand pays per token, batch is discounted, and Provisioned Throughput reserves capacity. Exam tip: models through an A P I is Bedrock, run agents is AgentCore, and managed R A G is Knowledge Bases.

1.title: Look-Alikes: Customizing and Evaluating Models
1.text: Next, customization and evaluation. R A G brings in your documents at question time; fine-tuning uses labeled pairs; continued pre-training uses unlabeled domain text. Distillation moves knowledge from a large teacher to a small student; R L H F uses human rankings; transfer learning reuses a model for a related task. In prompts, zero-shot uses no examples, few-shot uses examples, and chain-of-thought asks for steps. Rouge measures recall overlap, Bleu measures precision overlap, and Bert Score measures meaning. L L M as a judge scores fast, with reasons, and human evaluation judges subjective quality. Accuracy, precision, recall and F one measure classification. Exam tip: look at the data first. Is it labeled, unlabeled, teacher output or human ranking?

1.title: Look-Alikes: Responsible AI, Security and Governance
1.text: Now responsibility, security and governance look-alikes. Guardrails filters content, Clarify finds bias and explains predictions, and Model Cards document a model. Amazon A two I is human review of predictions, and Model Evaluation scores model quality. K M S manages encryption keys, Secrets Manager holds credentials, and Macie finds sensitive data in S three. PrivateLink is a private network path, and I A M decides who may do what. AgentCore Identity says who the agent is, and Policy says what it may do. Config records what changed, CloudTrail records who did it, and Inspector finds vulnerabilities. Artifact provides compliance reports, and Trusted Advisor checks best practices. Exam tip: CloudTrail records who, Config records what changed, and Inspector scans for flaws.

1.title: Service Chooser: Building AI Applications
1.text: Now the service chooser. Turn speech into text: Transcribe. Use a foundation model through an A P I: Bedrock. Build and train my own M L model: SageMaker A I. Answer from my own documents: Knowledge Bases, which is R A G. Store embeddings next to S Q L data: Aurora PostgreSQL with p g vector. Link entities and vectors: Neptune Analytics. Complete a multi-step task through A P I s: an agent, run on AgentCore. And save prompts, variants and versions: Prompt Management. Exam tip: name the verb in the need, then the service.

1.title: Service Chooser: Safe, Secure and Compliant
1.text: The second chooser covers safety, security and compliance. Block harmful content and mask P I I: Bedrock Guardrails. Catch ungrounded answers: a contextual grounding check. Detect bias in data and predictions: SageMaker Clarify. Document a model's purpose and risk: SageMaker Model Cards. Keep model traffic off the internet: PrivateLink. Find personal data in S three files: Amazon Macie. Show auditors A W S's compliance reports: A W S Artifact. And record who called which A P I: A W S CloudTrail. Exam tip: if two answers fit, choose the one that grants less access or needs less setup.

1.title: Lists the Exam Likes
1.text: Some lists are easy points. Inference types: real-time, serverless, asynchronous, batch. The M L lifecycle: business goal, framing, data processing, model development, deployment, monitoring. The foundation model lifecycle: data selection, model selection, pre-training, fine-tuning, evaluation, deployment, feedback. Customization, cheapest first: prompts, R A G, fine-tuning, distillation, pre-training. Responsible A I features: bias, fairness, inclusivity, robustness, safety, veracity. And the Scoping Matrix scopes: consumer app, enterprise app, pre-trained, fine-tuned, self-trained. Exam tip: lists are easy points, so say each one aloud from memory.

1.title: Terms That Trip People Up
1.text: Finally, terms that trip people up. A hallucination is a confident wrong answer; nondeterminism is different answers to the same prompt. Temperature sets randomness, Top K sets a fixed number of candidates, and Top P sets a share of probability. A token is a piece of text, a chunk is a split piece of a document, and an embedding is a vector of meaning. Transparent is about how a model was built, and explainable is about why it answered. Grounding ties answers to sources, and source citation shows which sources. Precision means few false alarms, and recall means few misses. Exam tip: when two terms look alike, say the one-line difference before you answer.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. One page: five domains, sixty-five questions, ninety minutes, and seven hundred to pass. Look-alikes: learn the one-line job of each idea and service, because the exam describes the job. The chooser: name the verb in the need, then the service. The lists: inference types, lifecycles, the customization ladder, responsible A I features and the scoping matrix. And the terms: hallucination, temperature, token, chunk, embedding, transparent, explainable and grounding. Next, Module sixteen covers exam technique and your final review.
